notes.title: Dev log #3: Let's talk about the career mode
notes.content:
[h2][b]Hello, players![/b][/h2][p]Today, we’re diving into a key aspect of our game — one that sets it apart from all other racing sims on the market: Career Mode.[/p][p]It’s a huge topic, and we won’t cover every detail today — there’s enough here for several dedicated articles. For now, we want to give you a general overview of what gameplay in this mode will look like. Let’s start with a look at the main menu of Career Mode (keep in mind: this is a concept art, so the final version will look different):[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45478868/309138f2156efe94bbd92dae2d2852f1f96c24ce.png"][/img][/p][h2][/h2][h2][b]Buy, modify, repair… and hunt for bargains[/b][/h2][p]Your journey begins at the [b]Used Car Dealership[/b], where you’ll pick your starter car. You’ll be coming back here regularly as the offer changes frequently and features randomly generated vehicles: each car will come with its own unique set of parts (bodywork, engine, chassis, interior, etc.), and of course, you’ll need to deal with various defects: from a dented fender, to a leaky engine or a rusted exhaust (remember, if your car is too loud, you won’t be allowed to race!), all the way to aggressive rust eating away at the sills and frame.
[/p][p]Once you’ve bought your dream ride (or just whatever you could afford), you’ll head to your [b]Garage… [/b]or straight to the [b]Workshop[/b]. Both places let you repair and modify your car — simpler jobs (like replacing most parts) can be done by yourself in the Garage, but for more complex issues you’ll need help from the Workshop. Keep in mind that some operations (especially major repairs) can take a week or more to complete, so your newly bought ride may not be race-ready right away.[/p][p]
Of course, to replace any parts, you’ll need to buy them first. Where from? Most items will be available instantly through the online store, but bargain hunters can also visit the [b]Parts Marketplace[/b]. Just like with the Used Car Dealership, the Marketplace’s offer refreshes regularly and randomly. You may find there unique used parts not available in the standard store — especially body parts for models that haven’t been produced in years. Sure, the tires may be a bit worn and the bumper might not match your car’s color (the [b]Paint Shop[/b] can help with that), but the prices should be more attractive.[/p][p] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45478868/ade90f4429574e1b1073e202c911445536e6269e.png"][/img][/p][h2][/h2][h2][b]Get behind the wheel![/b][/h2][p]Enough talk about buying and modding — it’s time to drive! If you’re feeling confident, the [b]Race Central[/b] is where you want to go. At first, you’ll visit the National Race Central to take part in amateur competition like time attack and autocross — that is, racing against the clock on circuits or point-to-point courses (marked with cones, barrels, etc.).
[/p][p]If you’re not ready to race just yet, head to the [b]Academy[/b]. From here, you’ll be able to visit tracks and practice chosen layouts — or just explore open maps in freeroam mode. This is also where you’ll attend paid lessons to earn [b]licenses [/b]in a discipline of your choice (circuit racing, rallycross, drift), which are required to enter professional events available through the International and World Race Centrals.[/p][p] [/p][h2][b]Summary[/b][/h2][p]That’s the general idea of how gameplay in Career Mode will look. In future dev blogs, we’ll dive deeper into individual mechanics — and much more.[/p][p][/p][p]That leaves us with the most important question: when can you play Career Mode? Sadly, we’re still not ready to talk about a release date of the game, but we’ll give you a taste of what we’re working on for this mode before the full launch.[/p][p][/p][p]There’s still a lot more to reveal about Track Day, so check back regularly. You can also join us on Discord and Patreon if you want to follow the project more closely.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]P.S.[/b][/h3][p]You’ll be able to meet us again this coming weekend — at two different events happening simultaneously in Poland: Retro Motor Show (Sept 19–21) and the final round of the Polish Car Racing Championships at Tor Poznań (Sept 20–21).[/p][p][/p][p]The latter might be especially interesting — because a unique competition will be taking place there. Our partners from Sim-Center are bringing two motion simulators (5 DOF), used to host a time attack competition. Whoever sets the best time will be invited by Drive Squad (our partners as well) to a real-world Super S Cup test session for the 2026 season — a rare opportunity to go from simracing to the real thing![/p]

notes.title: Dev log #2: Let’s talk about cars
notes.content:
[h3]As we mentioned recently, it's time to talk about the game itself again, rather than the events where we promote it (although, coincidentally, you'll find us again this upcoming weekend at Tor Poznań during the Polish Racing Car Championships).[/h3][h3][/h3][h3]Today, we're going to discuss a fundamental matter: cars. After all, that's why we're here, right?
[/h3][h3]During conversations with players, we often hear questions not only about which models will be in the game (it's still too early to provide a specific list), but also whether we'll even have licensed vehicles. This is a very interesting topic — and not as obvious as it might seem.[/h3][p][/p][h3]While the final decision on this matter has not yet been made, at this moment we are leaning towards using unlicensed cars in the game. Two main factors are driving this decision: money (duh!) and creative freedom.
[/h3][h3]The first is self-explanatory: car manufacturers charge a fee for using their trademarks. The money we'd pay them couldn't then be invested, for example, in the work of programmers, which could result in a better driving model or more diverse gameplay.[/h3][h3][/h3][h3]And creative freedom? You might not realize it, but rights holders sometimes have objections to what happens with their properties in games. In the context of racing games, this primarily concerns vehicle damage — manufacturers generally don't want their cars depicted as smoking wrecks. Since amateur racing frequently involves cars turning into smoking wrecks, we don't want to lose the freedom to smash them into pieces. Don't expect a destruction system as spectacular as in BeamNG.drive or the Wreckfest series (after all, damage is the essence of those games and requires a huge amount of work from entire teams), but crashes in Track Day will still sting. On a side note: it's no coincidence that games I mentioned only feature fictional vehicles.[/h3][h3][/h3][h3]And to avoid misunderstandings: just because our cars won't be licensed doesn't mean they won't be authentic. We are, after all, creating a simulator, so we want to reproduce individual vehicles as realistically as possible. We'll achieve this by scanning them and refining their handling with the involvement of people who race them (we have such contacts thanks to the support of the Automobile Club of Greater Poland, for example). The only things missing will be the specific brand names and logos. But surely, we can live without that, right? And anyone interested will likely still know what car it is:
[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45478868/1b51a48e70bc5547935bbb0fffbd642ac5a4e433.png"][/img]
[/p][h3]Share your thoughts on this in the comments!
[/h3][h3](BTW, a friendly reminder in case you missed our previous announcement: you can find Track Day on [url="https://www.patreon.com/c/Szymik" style="button" buttoncolor="#ff0000"]Patreon[/url]! By supporting our game you can get some exclusive mods for Assetto Corsa, starting with Tor Poznań 2025. More content to follow very soon!)[/h3]

notes.title: We’re launching Patreon with Tor Poznań 2025
notes.content:
[h3]Hello, players!
[/h3][h3]After packing up our stand at Tor Poznań, where the Drive Squad racing team hosted us last weekend during the Polish Car Racing Championships (WSMP in Polish), we've returned home with renewed motivation and a strong resolve to take the next step in the development of Track Day.
[/h3][h3]For two days, we offered an updated version of the Tor Poznań track for testing (on a sim rig provided by Sim-Center) and spoke with dozens of people – professional racing drivers from Poland and the Czech Republic, simracers, and motorsport enthusiasts – all of whom expressed keen interest in what we're creating.
[/h3][h3]That's why today we've launched [url="patreon.com/Szymik" style="button"]Patreon[/url]. Anyone who wishes can support us choosing one of the available tiers, and all funds raised will be allocated to the production of Track Day. This will allow us to maintain independence and complete creative control over this unique project, which is being developed against current trends in the gaming industry.[/h3][h3]
[/h3][h3]Of course, we'll reward your support with various benefits. To start, and to keep things simple, we're offering two tiers:[/h3][list][*][p]Pit Crew - $1 per month - grants access to a special room on our Discord server.[/p][/*][*][p]Test Driver - $4 per month - allows you to download Tor Poznań 2025 for Assetto Corsa (an updated, improved version of our mod), and provides access to an exclusive server featuring this track.
[/p][/*][/list][h3]Over time, we'll add more options and benefits as we achieve further milestones in Track Day's development.[/h3][p]
[/p][h3]Thank you in advance for your support, and we'll be in touch soon![/h3]

notes.title: Polish tracks: Autodrom Słomczyn
notes.content:
[h2]Hello, players!
[/h2]
It's been more than two weeks since we officially announced Track Day, and we're seeing constant growth of interest with the game around the globe. We’d like to thank Overtake.gg and all other media outlets for covering our project, as well as players for wishlisting it!

To celebrate this ongoing success we decided to publish another… Well, this time it’s not exactly a dev log. We’d like to use this space to promote Polish tracks which aren’t lucky enough to be featured in “international” racing games (apart from mods). It’s part of the reason why we’re creating Track Day.

[h2]So today we’re introducing to you the Autodrom Słomczyn.[/h2]

Located near Poland's capital city of Warsaw and created in 1994, Słomczyn is a relatively small circuit (the main course for karts has 1,2 km) but it comes with multiple layouts and sees lots of action. It hosts FIA CEZ rallycross events, kart racing, drifting competition, time attacks, and even serves as a special stage for the famous Barbórka Rally. And while the track’s surface is basically flat, there is a proper jump on the gravel section.

Take a look at our footage from Autodrom Słomczyn:

notes.title: Dev Log #1: The heart of Tor Poznań
notes.content:
[b]Hello, players![/b]

[h2]We're overwhelmed with your warm reception of Track Day, and we're very grateful for it! Thank you!
[/h2]
While we’re getting ready to show you more footage from the game, we'd like to give you a glimpse of our preparations for creating tracks for Track Day.

The first location to be released with the future demo version of Track Day will be Tor Poznań. It's the biggest and most renowned race track in Poland, opened in the 1970s and destined for hosting F1 races (which, sadly, never happened).

While we already have the main layouts of Tor Poznań (full course and karting track) ready, we still need to fill it with highly detailed areas inside the track.

These will be used for exploring, test driving, and racing, naturally. Technical roads and squares are perfect for creating a wide range of technical point-to-point routes for fierce amateur competition. Below you can see some of our reference shots for artists, captured during a recent event called SuperOES.

notes.title: An introduction to Track Day
notes.content:
Welcome, dear players! Welcome to Track Day!

[h2][b]Who are you and what is this?[/b][/h2]

We're a small, independent development team from Poland. We love cars and racing, and while we conceived this project fairly recently, [b]we've been actually preparing to create Track Day for years.[/b] We did so by releasing mods for Assetto Corsa (like [url=https://www.overtake.gg/downloads/tor-pozna%C5%84.6118/]Tor Poznan[/url] , created by the leader of our team, Krzysztof “Szymik” Szymikowski), participating in track days or kart racing, and simply by playing and studying racing games. We felt more and more tired with creative stagnation in our beloved genre in recent years, and we finally decided to do something about it.

[b]We wanted to take a new approach to driving cars, upgrading them and living the life of a race driver[/b]  who aims to reach the top. Sure, it's a theme you've seen in hundreds of games, but this time it will be different. You'll be driving different cars on [b]different tracks (designed as maps for freeroaming)[/b] than in most games, starting with the lowest low and climbing gradually to reach... well, if not the top then at least some heights of motorsport. 

But before you achieve anything in racing, you’ll need to prove your skills in contests for amateurs and then become a professional, licensed driver. Then earn some cash and prepare your car thoroughly. Then win some races… and try not to go broke when you’ll get an invoice for repairs and sets of fresh tires. And when you make a name for yourself in Poland and other parts of Central Europe eventually, you can take the fight to the Western Europe and maybe even further.

The game is inspired by the reality of car racing in Poland. It’s a harsh but interesting reality and we wanted to give you an authentic experience of it. However, it doesn’t necessarily mean that Track Day is a hardcore sim. [b]We wish to give you an accessible, customizable game[/b] where you can adjust the gameplay to your preferences by lowering or raising the difficulty level to your heart’s content (as well as making rules more or less complex). We’ll also explain the world of racing to newcomers with our RPG-inspired dialogue system. At the end of the day, Track Day is about having fun first and foremost.

[h2][b]Cool! When can I play it?[/b][/h2]

That's the difficult question. We have big ambitions and tons of ideas for features to implement in Track Day, but our ability to make them real depends on getting funds for development. We're actively looking for inverstors willing to support us in realizing our vision. You, players, can help us reach that goal too by supporting the project (join us on Discord via the link below for more details on that), and you’ll be among the first to taste the upcoming demo version.

[b]Next step is to release Track Day in Early Access[/b]. However, we won't do it until we have the career mode with core features completed (some of those mentioned on the Steam page may be missing at launch) and at least the minimum amount of essential content (cars, tracks, etc.). We're going to add more features and content over time. For example, we'd like to provide VR support but it depends on the success we achieve with Track Day in Early Access.

At this point we don’t specify goals for the 1.0 release of Track Day. [b]Our vision for the game allows us to expand it nearly infinitely. [/b]For example, when we feel we're done with European racing, we could go forth to visit America and other parts of the world. Your feedback will be crucial to determine our next steps. Therefore we invite you to take part in this automotive adventure with us and to shape the future of Track Day together.

You can begin with joining us on Discord:
[url=https://discord.com/invite/cJeDYxGZ4v]https://discord.com/invite/cJeDYxGZ4v[/url]
